blindSummary: Research located no state/province-specific statute, enforcement series, or event finding for this unit; the sources describe only the national framework, which applies here in full.
blindSourceSummaries: Official state-gazette text of the 2023 trans-equality law (in force from 1 March 2023): self-declaration legal gender recognition without medical diagnosis, public-authority equality duties and a national LGBT equality strategy - the unitary statutory framework every state/province, including this one, operates under.

An international human-rights organisation's news article (16 Feb 2023): hails the new law's passage through parliament as a landmark for trans rights - self-declaration gender recognition, anti-discrimination protections - while noting backlash; context for the national framework applied uniformly across states/provinces.

A criminal-law firm analysis (June 2026, updated Sept 2026) on hate-crime and LGBT protection: disentangles the three statutes commonly confused - what the 2023 equality law does and does not do; the penal code's discrimination aggravating factor covering gender-identity motives; the hate-offences provision and its penalties - and notes 'gender expression' is an absent term in the criminal code; applies to enforcement in every state/province including this one.
